newsitem.title: UK: Standard Chartered Bank wins and loses on forex.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered Bank wins and loses on forex.

text.p: Standard Chartered, the London-based bank with a big Asia-Pacific region franchise, Wednesday reported first-half pre-tax profits of 435 million pounds ($707 million), seriously affected by the strength of the British pound.

The latest results compared with profits of 448 million pounds ($728 million) last year, but that included an exceptional gain of 46 million pounds ($75 million), while operating profit was up 8 percent but would have risen 16 percent if exchange rates had remained constant.
At the same time, Standard Chartered reported big profits from foreign exchange trading in the Far East, where currency turmoil has been particularly strong in recent months.
Chief Executive Malcolm Williamson told Reuters the bank had not experienced such a big effect on its profits from translation into sterling before.

"The problem we have ... is that we are very much a dollar-related bank. We either get our money in U.S. dollars or currencies that are linked to it or currencies that have depreciated even more against sterling over the last year," Williamson said.

At constant exchange rates, the bank's operating profit would have risen by 16 percent. But it gained by only 8 percent to 434 million pounds ($706 million), compared with 402 million pounds ($654 million)in the first half of 1996.
The bank used a sterling/dollar rate of 1.67 for the first half of this year, compared with 1.55 this time last year.
Williamson calculated that a rough rule of thumb is that the bank loses around 50 million pounds ($81 million) on reported profit figures for every 1 percent change in the exchange rate.
But he pointed out that this was a rough calculation because the figures are affected both on the costs and income side and in the latter are affected by the mix of assets on the balance sheet.
Williamson dismissed as "absolutely untrue" recent rumours in the foreign exchange markets that Standard Chartered had lost money in the volatility.
"We've had a very good record on this in the last few months," he said. "You get daily ups and downs, but we've managed our book tightly and well and it's continued through July."
